advances: The proposed half-gluing inequality for complete positive affine-root tables is false. There is an exact sequence of full-dimensional rational base polytopes and positive affine roots for which the maximum final full-incidence packing is 1, the integral of the maximum layer packing is (m+1)/2, and their ratio is 2/(m+1), tending to zero. Every layer target and every possible final integer target are evaluated. This obstructs the proposed moving-target layer bridge. It does not disprove the registered uniform affine-root lower bound or the locked weak Oertel conjecture.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The original full-incidence packing and arbitrary-support conventions are supplied by accepted fact `793210f8a4be3647`; the canonical logarithmic notation and the separate integral hitting quantities are supplied by accepted fact `488f0a583886b5fc`. All geometry, complete-support verification, all-target packing evaluations, and quantitative layer calculations are proved above.
proof:
Fix \(m\ge1\). Write a base point as \((z,u)\in\mathbb R^{m-1}\times\mathbb R\). Let \(b_1=0\), and, for \(2\le i\le m\), let \(b_i=e_{i-1}\), where the latter are the standard coordinate vectors of \(\mathbb R^{m-1}\). For \(m=1\), \(\mathbb R^0\) has its single point \(b_1\). Put

\[
N_i=2^i-1,\qquad a_i=2^{-i}\quad(1\le i\le m).
\]

On the standard simplex

\[
\Sigma=\{z\in\mathbb R^{m-1}:z\ge0,\ \textstyle\sum_{h=1}^{m-1}z_h\le1\},
\]

use its barycentric coordinates

\[
\beta_1(z)=1-\sum_{h=1}^{m-1}z_h,
\qquad
\beta_i(z)=z_{i-1}\quad(2\le i\le m).
\]

Define

\[
P_m=\left\{(z,u):z\in\Sigma,\quad
\left|u\right|\le\sum_{i=1}^m\beta_i(z)N_i\right\},
\qquad
L_m(z,u)=\sum_{i=1}^m\beta_i(z)a_i.
\tag{1}
\]

Here \(L_m\) is exactly the positive affine function called L in the bounded task, not a packing cutoff or a root-volume cost. Its values are not a renormalization of the weights. The set \(P_m\) is also the convex hull of the m intervals \(\{b_i\}\times[-N_i,N_i]\): one containment follows by taking convex combinations, and the reverse follows by writing a permitted u as the same convex combination of suitable interval coordinates. Equivalently, the displayed affine inequalities directly show that it is a compact rational convex polytope. It has full dimension m. For example, its vertex interval at \(b_1\) has a nonzero difference in the u direction, and differences to one point on each of the other vertex intervals span all m-1 marker directions. For \(m=1\), it is simply \([-1,1]\).

Since the \(\beta_i\) are nonnegative and sum to one on \(\Sigma\),

\[
2^{-m}\le L_m(z,u)\le\frac12\quad((z,u)\in P_m).
\]

In particular \(C_m\) is compact and is specified by rational affine inequalities. It is convex because both inequalities \(\pm y\le L_m(z,u)/2\) are affine inequalities. The interior of \(P_m\), together with sufficiently small y, gives nonempty interior in \(\mathbb R^{m+1}\). Thus \(C_m\) is a full-dimensional rational convex polytope of precisely the actual-body form required by the task.

The only integer points of \(\Sigma\) are \(b_1,\ldots,b_m\): an integer nonnegative vector whose coordinate sum is at most one is either zero or a standard coordinate vector. Hence the complete integer support, including the endpoints of every interval, is

\[
D=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^m D_i,
\qquad
D_i=\{(b_i,j):j\in\mathbb Z,\ -N_i\le j\le N_i\}.
\tag{2}
\]

At every index in \(D_i\), the actual vertical fiber of \(C_m\) is the interval \([-a_i/2,a_i/2]\), with original volume \(w_{(b_i,j)}=a_i\). Every other integer fiber is empty. Therefore no integer site or positive boundary fiber has been omitted. Summing these original weights gives

\[
W=\sum_{i=1}^m(2N_i+1)a_i
=\sum_{i=1}^m(2-2^{-i})
=2m-1+2^{-m}.
\tag{3}
\]

For any barycentric component with integer target \(\mathbf J\in D\), affinity of \(L_m\) gives

\[
\sum_{\mathbf I\in E}\lambda_{\mathbf I}w_{\mathbf I}^{1/d}
=\sum_{\mathbf I\in E}\lambda_{\mathbf I}L_m(\mathbf I)
=L_m(\mathbf J)=w_{\mathbf J},\qquad d=1.
\]

Thus its canonical root-volume cost from `793210f8a4be3647` is exactly zero, for every positive support and coefficient vector. The unrestricted fractional score consequently obeys
\(\mathcal B_1(w)=\max_{\mathbf J\in D}P_1(\mathbf J,0)\).

We now account for every possible target and every possible support. Fix \(\mathbf J=(b_i,j)\in D_i\). If a positive barycentric combination of sources in D has marker barycenter \(b_i\), all of those sources have marker \(b_i\). Indeed, if \(i=1\), all marker coordinates of every source are nonnegative, so a positive combination equal to zero can only use zero markers. If \(i\ge2\), the \((i-1)\)-st marker coordinate of the barycenter is one, whereas this coordinate of every source is either zero or one. Positivity and sum one force every source to have this coordinate one, and the only such marker is \(b_i\). Hence every component at \(\mathbf J\) uses only sources in \(D_i\). This applies to arbitrary arity and excludes every component crossing distinct groups.

Suppose all auxiliary capacities on \(D_i\) equal a nonnegative number c. Capacities on other groups have no effect on \(T_{(b_i,j)}\). We claim the exact full-incidence value is

\[
T_{(b_i,j)}(v)=c\bigl(N_i+1-|j|\bigr).
\tag{4}
\]

For the upper bound, every positive support with barycenter j contains a coordinate at most j and a coordinate at least j. Otherwise all its coordinates would be strictly greater than j, or all would be strictly less than j. This includes the singleton \(\{(b_i,j)\}\) and all equality cases. Consequently each of the two sets

\[
F_- =\{(b_i,h)\in D_i:h\le j\},
\qquad
F_+ =\{(b_i,h)\in D_i:h\ge j\}
\]

meets every component at \((b_i,j)\). For either F and any feasible full-incidence scheme,

\[
\sum_E x_E
\le\sum_E |E\cap F|x_E
=\sum_{\mathbf I\in F}\sum_{E\ni\mathbf I}x_E
\le\sum_{\mathbf I\in F}v_{\mathbf I}.
\]

The same inequality applies directly to a finite scheme of arbitrary positive supports. The two cardinalities are \(N_i+j+1\) and \(N_i-j+1\), respectively. Taking their smaller capacity sum proves the upper bound in (4). This is a direct source-capacity inequality; no rounding of an integral cover is used to lower-bound the packing.

For the matching lower bound, there are \(N_i+j\) integer coordinates strictly below j and \(N_i-j\) strictly above j. Match every coordinate on the smaller side injectively to coordinates on the larger side. This produces \(N_i-|j|\) disjoint pairs \(\{(b_i,h),(b_i,k)\}\), with \(h<j<k\). Give such a pair coefficients

\[
\lambda_h=\frac{k-j}{k-h}>0,
\qquad
\lambda_k=\frac{j-h}{k-h}>0.
\]

Their sum is one and their barycenter is \((b_i,j)\). Give each pair mass c and also give the central singleton mass c. Every used source is charged exactly c, because the pairs are disjoint and exclude the singleton source; all unused sources are charged zero. This is a feasible scheme in the original full-incidence program, of mass \(c(N_i-|j|+1)\). It proves (4), also when \(c=0\), when the smaller side is empty, or when j is an endpoint. Pair constructions here certify the lower bound of an exactly evaluated unrestricted program; the all-arity upper bound has already been proved.

For the original weights, take \(c=a_i=2^{-i}\) in (4). At every possible final target,

\[
P_1((b_i,j),0)=2^{-i}(2^i-|j|)\le1,
\tag{5}
\]

with equality at \((b_i,0)\) for every i. Thus the maximum over the entire D is exactly 1, not a bound at a prescribed target.

For a layer t, all capacities in group \(D_i\) are equal to \(c_i(t)=\mathbf1_{\{2^{-i}\ge t\}}\). Equation (4) gives every layer target value, including all targets in inactive groups:

\[
T_{(b_i,j)}(v(t))
=\mathbf1_{\{2^{-i}\ge t\}}(2^i-|j|).
\tag{6}
\]

For \(1\le i<m\) and \(2^{-(i+1)}<t\le2^{-i}\), the active groups are exactly \(D_1,\ldots,D_i\), and the layer maximum is \(2^i\), attained at \((b_i,0)\). For \(0<t\le2^{-m}\), all groups are active, and the layer maximum is \(2^m\), attained at \((b_m,0)\). For \(t>1/2\), the layer maximum is zero. At equality thresholds the stated weak inequality includes the group of that threshold; changes at finitely many thresholds do not affect the integral. Thus all moving layer targets are allowed integer indices of the same complete D. Direct integration gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_0^\infty\max_{\mathbf J\in D}T_{\mathbf J}(v(t))\,dt
&=\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}2^i\bigl(2^{-i}-2^{-(i+1)}\bigr)
+2^m2^{-m}\\
&=\frac{m-1}{2}+1=\frac{m+1}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]

Together, (5) and (7) prove the exact ratio in the statement. In particular the proposed half-gluing right side is \((m+1)/4>1\) whenever \(m\ge4\).

For completeness, retain the canonical logarithmic normalization of `488f0a583886b5fc`, without changing the original w or W. Here

\[
w_{\max}=\frac12,
\qquad
\phi_{(b_i,j)}=\log\frac{w_{\max}}{w_{(b_i,j)}}=(i-1)\log2,
\qquad
B=(m-1)\log2.
\]

All positive barycentric supports at a fixed target remain in its one group, as proved above. Consequently \(G_E=\sum_{\mathbf I\in E}\lambda_{E,\mathbf I}\phi_{\mathbf I}-\phi_{\mathbf J}=0\) for every \(E\in\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}\). Thus the logarithmic zero-cutoff family is the entire family, and every nonnegative logarithmic cutoff has this same family. The disjoint pairs and central singleton used above force an integral hitting set to contain at least \(N_i-|j|+1\) distinct sources. Either \(F_-\) or \(F_+\) attains that number. Therefore, with their original integral meanings,

\[
m_{\log}((b_i,j),L;w)=a_i(N_i+1-|j|)\quad(L\ge0),
\qquad
\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)=1.
\]

This separate evaluation is not used to establish the fractional lower bounds.

Closed base halfspaces realizing these hitting upper bounds can also be displayed with all equality atoms included. Define \(f_1(z)=\sum_h z_h\) and, for \(i\ge2\), \(f_i(z)=1-z_{i-1}\). At the allowed markers, \(f_i(b_i)=0\) and \(f_i(b_h)=1\) for \(h\ne i\). Choose a real \(A>N_m+|j|\). The two closed base halfspaces

\[
\{-A f_i(z)+j-u\ge0\},
\qquad
\{-A f_i(z)+u-j\ge0\}
\]

contain precisely \(F_-\) and \(F_+\), respectively, among the atoms D. Their scores at \((b_i,j)\) equal zero. For \(m=1\), take \(f_1=0\), giving the usual two interval cuts. These have nonzero base normals and extend to vertical ambient halfspaces by giving y coefficient zero; they include every atom at equality, including the whole fiber at the target. Thus no boundary-atom deletion or exclusion of vertical normals enters this construction.

Finally, the normalization relevant to the original registered affine-root subgoal is

\[
\frac{\max_{\mathbf J\in D}P_1(\mathbf J,0)}{W/2^n}
=\frac{2^m}{2m-1+2^{-m}},\qquad n=m.
\]

It tends to infinity. Hence this sequence refutes the bounded half-gluing claim, with a vanishing gluing ratio, while leaving the registered absolute-constant lower bound for the whole affine-root class unresolved. In particular it is not a counterexample to the locked mixed-integer depth statement.
statement:
Use the original full-occurrence packing conventions of accepted fact `793210f8a4be3647`. Thus, for an actual positive table w on its complete positive integer support D, the finite family \(\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}\) consists of the nonempty affinely independent source sets with \(\mathbf J\) in the relative interior of their convex hull. For nonnegative auxiliary capacities v on D, define

\[
T_{\mathbf J}(v)=\max\left\{\sum_{E\in\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}}x_E:
x_E\ge0,\quad
\sum_{\substack{E\in\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}\\\mathbf I\in E}}x_E\le v_{\mathbf I}\quad(\mathbf I\in D)\right\}.
\]

In particular, each participating source is charged the full component mass. The arbitrary-positive-support interpretation has the same value, by the support reduction of `793210f8a4be3647`; no restriction to pair supports is imposed in the definition. All roots in the following instances are affine, so \(P_d(\mathbf J,0)=T_{\mathbf J}(w)\).

For every integer \(m\ge1\), there is an instance with \(n=m\), \(d=1\), a full-dimensional compact rational convex polytope \(P_m\subset\mathbb R^m\), and an affine function \(L_m>0\) on \(P_m\), whose actual body is

\[
C_m=\{(x,y):x\in P_m,\ |y|\le L_m(x)/2\}.
\]

Its complete integer support is \(D=P_m\cap\mathbb Z^m\), its original weights are \(w_{\mathbf I}=L_m(\mathbf I)\), and its original total mixed volume is

\[
W=\mathcal H_1(C_m\cap(\mathbb Z^m\times\mathbb R))
=2m-1+2^{-m}.
\]

For \(v_{\mathbf I}(t)=\mathbf1_{\{w_{\mathbf I}\ge t\}}\), these instances satisfy

\[
\max_{\mathbf J\in D}P_1(\mathbf J,0)=1,
\qquad
\int_0^\infty\max_{\mathbf J\in D}T_{\mathbf J}(v(t))\,dt=\frac{m+1}{2}.
\]

Consequently their gluing ratios are exactly

\[
\frac{\max_{\mathbf J\in D}P_1(\mathbf J,0)}
{\displaystyle\int_0^\infty\max_{\mathbf J\in D}T_{\mathbf J}(v(t))\,dt}
=\frac2{m+1}\longrightarrow0.
\]

The proposed factor 1/2 inequality fails for every \(m\ge4\). In fact no positive absolute factor can replace 1/2 in that inequality for this affine-root class.

The normalized potential \(\phi\), its amplitude \(B\), the gaps \(G_E\), and the integral quantities \(m_{\log}\) and \(\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}\) retain the meanings of `488f0a583886b5fc`. They are evaluated below without replacing fractional packing by integral hitting. Neither conditional assignment entropy \(H(r)\) nor target entropy \(S(q)\) is needed or redefined.
